Coca-Cola (KO) has surged 35% in 2026, posting five straight earnings beats and raising its full-year EPS guidance to a range of 9 to 10%.

PepsiCo (PEP) is down 3% and Monster Beverage (MNST) up 23% YTD, both well behind Coca-Cola's company-specific outperformance.

At 31x earnings, KO's rich valuation faces a pivotal test on October 27, with IRS risk and weaker lower-income consumers as headwinds.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

A century-old beverage giant has become one of the more surprising stock-market winners of 2026, running ahead of faster-growing rivals. Coca-Cola (NYSE:KO) stock is down 0.6% to $92.83 in afternoon trading, a modest dip against a 35% gain year to date (YTD).

Image by Rob Hayek via 24/7 Wall Street

A surge this large from a mature consumer staple puts shareholders in a tough spot. The hold case rests on Coca-Cola's defensive appeal, but a gain this large leaves less room for disappointment, the heart of the profit-taking argument.

Coca-Cola Outruns Its Beverage Rivals

Coca-Cola stock has pulled well ahead of its two closest beverage peers. Notably, PepsiCo (NASDAQ:PEP) stock is down 3% to $134.46 YTD. Monster Beverage (NASDAQ:MNST) stock is up 23% to $46.98 YTD, still behind Coca-Cola.

Each company runs a distinct business model. For its part, Coca-Cola sells concentrate and syrups to bottlers and owns brands including Sprite, Fanta, Powerade and BODYARMOR, while PepsiCo pairs beverages with a large snack business. Energy drinks are the focus at Monster.

Defensive Demand Explains Only Part of the Rally

A search for steadier names has supported consumer staples this year. The Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF (NYSEARCA:XLP) is up 15% to $87.59 YTD, short of the gain in Coca-Cola stock. Coca-Cola shares made up 6.8% of the fund's net assets as of June 30, one of its largest positions.

One e-commerce platform has pulled sharply away from its peers, and the size of that lead has turned a strong rally into a harder decision for shareholders. Shares of Shopify (NASDAQ:SHOP) are up 35% over the past month to $173.81, and they're climbing 2% in afternoon trading.

Shopify stock's run comes from two forces: a quarter of rapid growth and a steady climb in Wall Street's earnings forecasts. A gain this large raises a fair question about whether Shopify stock has more room to run or whether it's time to lock in some profits. The answer depends on how much weight investors put on growth versus valuation.

A Rally Built on Shopify Alone

Other e-commerce stocks have fell behind. For example, shares of MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) are up 5% over the past month to $1,868.19, a far smaller advance than the gain in Shopify shares.

Online retail funds have generally fallen behind SHOP stock during the past month. Shares of the Amplify Online Retail ETF (NYSEARCA:IBUY) are up 6% over the past month to $71.36. As a tech-sector gauge, the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 0.3% over the past month to $719.15, which marks the rally in Shopify stock as company-specific.

Shopify's business model sets it apart from both comparisons. The company sells subscription software and payment services to merchants that run their own online stores, while MercadoLibre runs a Latin American e-commerce and payments marketplace.

A renewed debate over whether specialized AI cloud providers can pay for their buildouts is creating volatility in IREN Limited (NASDAQ:IREN) stock, even after a direct reassurance from its co-CEO. In morning trading, IREN stock declined 6% to $26.15 before recovering to $27.41, down only 1%.

cbowns / BY-SA 2.0

Meanwhile, TeraWulf (NASDAQ:WULF) shares are up 3% to $12.38. Applied Digital (NASDAQ:APLD) stock is trading at $19.86, also up 3%. TeraWulf and Applied Digital, like IREN, began as crypto miners before pivoting toward AI and high-performance computing infrastructure.

As a sector gauge, the CoinShares Bitcoin Mining and Digital Power ETF (NASDAQ:WGMI), which counts IREN, TeraWulf and Applied Digital among its holdings, is up 2% to $32.31. Large-cap tech is up moderately, with the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) up 0.34% to $720.77. That spread sets the volatility in IREN stock apart from anything the broader tech market could account for.

Forecaster's Warning Revives Neocloud Doubts

Neocloud is the industry's label for newer providers. These providers rent graphics processing unit (GPU) computing power to AI developers, and IREN's direct cloud rental business places it squarely in that group. In a CNBC interview on Monday, John Lovelock, chief analyst at a major technology research firm, stated that current AI returns don't support the scale of the neocloud buildout. Lovelock stood by his firm's report last week warning that most neocloud providers may not remain independent by the end of the decade.

Debt-funded AI cloud providers are back under pressure as concerns about borrowing costs spread across the group. First of all, CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) shares are down 4% to $58.67 in morning trading.

Andriy Onufriyenko / Moment via Getty Images

Moreover, Nebius Group (NASDAQ:NBIS) shares are falling harder, down 5% to $162.20. However, Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) stock is only down 0.52% to $128.95, a comparatively steady contrast to the slide in CoreWeave and Nebius shares.

That split shows strain concentrated in the most debt-reliant corner of AI infrastructure, where CoreWeave and Nebius both operate. With its far broader revenue base, Oracle stock sits outside the worst of the selling.

HSBC Doubles Down on Its Reduce Call

HSBC repeated its Reduce rating on CoreWeave in a note on Monday. The accompanying price target sits well below where CoreWeave shares last closed, leaving little doubt about the direction of that call.

CoreWeave's central challenge is revenue per megawatt of capacity, which could trail what larger cloud providers earn. Those bigger rivals offer broader services. They serve more diversified customers, giving them more ways to make money from each data center they run. Scale matters here, because bigger platforms can spread their costs across many products.

Two more pressure points weigh on CoreWeave. Slower growth at AI model developers could soften demand for short-term capacity, and rising borrowing costs make new infrastructure harder to finance.

title: Palantir Wins Knox Federal Partnership, Gains 4%
detail:
Palantir Wins Knox Federal Partnership, Gains 4%
Michael Douglass
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 1:20 PM MST 3 min read
PLTR
QQQ
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Palantir Wins Knox Federal Partnership, Gains 4% ©yangwenshuang from Getty Images Signature and Aflo Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Palantir shares rose 4% today after Knox Systems announced a partnership to bring commercial software into FedRAMP and IL5 federal environments.

The deal lets other companies' software reach the government through Palantir's federal accreditations, which makes Palantir more central to how agencies get new technology.

No financial terms were disclosed, and analysts already expect revenue to climb from $4.48 billion in 2025 to $8.22 billion in 2026.

The next test is the third-quarter report, which management guided to $2.16 billion to $2.164 billion of revenue.

Palantir Technologies (PLTR:NASDAQ) shares are up 4% today after Knox Systems announced a partnership, before Monday's open, to get commercial software into the government's most tightly secured clouds.

That wins back part of Friday's 7% drop, which pushed the stock into a correction. (Tech is having a good day, too: the QQQ QQQ:NASDAQ is up nearly 2%.)

What exactly happened

Knox, which is private, runs a managed federal cloud and says it can get software makers FedRAMP authorization in 90 days or less. It already hosts more than 100 AI and enterprise applications, for customers including Adobe (ADBE:NASDAQ), Sierra and Armis.

Palantir has already helped software companies deploy to federal agencies on its own accredited infrastructure, IL5 environments included. Put the two together, and a software maker gets one route from authorization to deployment.

As Knox CEO Irina Denisenko said in the press release: "Knox exists to get the best software in the world to the government faster, and to protect it once it's there."

Neither company disclosed financial terms.

Palantir becomes the on-ramp

Those accreditations are the hard part for any software maker selling to the Pentagon, and this deal puts Palantir's to work for other companies' products.

It also lands on top of a government business that's already flying. Palantir's U.S. government revenue rose 90% year over year to $809 million in Q2 2026, out of $1.94 billion in total revenue.

Analysts expect revenue to nearly double again this year, to $8.22 billion, and to reach $17.9 billion by 2028…

Palantir Technologies (PLTR): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023–2028 (TIKR)

With no terms disclosed, there's nothing in today's news for analysts to add to those estimates yet.

The multiple already came down

At Friday's close, Palantir traded at 98x forward earnings. That's a touch below its five-year average of 103x and far from the 270x it hit in October 2025…

Palantir Technologies (PLTR): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

Today's move puts it right back at that average. That's still a rich price, so the next real test is the third quarter, which management guided to $2.16 billion to $2.164 billion of revenue.

DeSantis vowed to legalize Tesla's flying Roadster in Florida, sending TSLA up 4% while RIVN and LCID each slipped about 1%.

QQQ's 2% tech rally explains part of Tesla's gain, but the Roadster pledge drove the extra boost above the broader market.

Federal regulators, not states, control flying vehicle approval, making DeSantis's pledge mostly symbolic with production still years away.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Tesla didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat TSLA. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

A pledge from Florida's governor is lifting one electric vehicle maker while its smaller rivals retreat. Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) shares are up 4% to $367.59 in afternoon trading after Florida Governor Ron DeSantis promised to make the company's flying Roadster legal in his state.

2023 Getty Images / Getty Images News via Getty Images
TSLA Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.

Meanwhile, Rivian Automotive (NASDAQ:RIVN) shares are down 0.9% to $12.31, trailing well behind the gain in Tesla shares, and Lucid Group (NASDAQ:LCID) is off by 1.12% to $3.10.

The divergence points to a reaction to the Roadster headline that's specific to Tesla, and Rivian and Lucid are smaller pure-play EV makers that aren't yet profitable.

DeSantis Pledges Florida Will Make the Roadster Legal

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis took to X. He declared that his state will make Tesla's flying Roadster legal, writing, "We will make sure that it's legal." His comments followed Tesla's revealing of the long-delayed Roadster last week.

At that event, a version of the Roadster fitted with air tanks and thrusters launched off a ramp, flew briefly and landed on its wheels. The demonstration turned a sports car Tesla has promised for years into a showcase for its engineering ambitions, and the governor's pledge now adds a political boost.

Tesla stock is also rising alongside a broad rebound in technology names, so the Roadster headline is one of two forces behind the move. Large-cap tech is strong, with the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) up 2%. That gap with Tesla stock suggests the Roadster pledge is giving Tesla an extra boost on top of the tech rally.

Tesla Pulls Away From Rivian and Lucid

The Global X Autonomous & Electric Vehicles ETF (NASDAQ:DRIV) is up 1%, a smaller advance than Tesla shares are posting. Its portfolio spans automakers, chipmakers, battery suppliers and autonomy software firms, which reduces the effect of any headline about a single company.

Rivian builds the R1T pickup, the R1S SUV and commercial electric delivery vans, and it's launching the mid-size R2 SUV to reach a broader market. Lucid designs the Air sedan and the Gravity SUV, assembling them in Arizona while preparing a second plant in Saudi Arabia for production. A software and services section, including a joint venture with Volkswagen Group, gives Rivian another source of revenue.

Closer to the governor's home state, Tesla runs its Robotaxi service in several U.S. metros, including unsupervised rides in Miami, Orlando and Tampa. That Florida presence gives the governor's endorsement extra weight for Tesla. Cybercab production has also begun at Tesla's Gigafactory Texas, and lines for the Optimus humanoid robot are being installed.

Roadster Hype Meets Regulatory Reality

Federal regulators decide whether a vehicle can fly, so Florida's endorsement carries mostly symbolic weight, and production isn't expected for years while Tesla hasn't announced a price for the flying version.

Optimists see the Roadster as evidence Tesla can still generate excitement around new hardware. However, a vehicle years from production and lacking federal clearance may add little to Tesla's near-term results. Tesla's growth pitch already leans on Full Self-Driving software, Megapack batteries and the Robotaxi service, leaving the Roadster at its edge.

TSLA Price Scenario — 24/7 Wall St.
Washington Holds the Key to the Flying Roadster

The next test for Tesla is whether the flying Roadster ever clears federal approval. Shareholders can watch for whether Florida officials follow up with details on how the state intends to honor the governor's pledge.

A rally in Tesla shares while Rivian and Lucid shares are slipping shows the Roadster headline lifting a single name in the EV group. Traders may prefer to keep their TSLA stock exposure reasonably small. It's wise to do so until the flying Roadster's path to production resolves, the kind of fenced-off speculation we spelled out in a free guide to small-stakes bets.
